How the network works

Every practice keeps its own brand. The connection lives underneath.

Patients will never see "an AMP practice." Each brand keeps its name, logo, website, Google profile and reviews, exactly as they are today. The network is built behind the scenes, in the places AI reads and patients don't: website code, AMP's own pages, shared clinical content and third‑party sources.

Code, not logosEach site's hidden schema markup names AMP as its parent organization. AI reads it; patients never see it.
Practice pages on weramp.comAMP's own site gives every practice a profile page that links out to the brand's website.
Shared clinical contentMDCodes and AMI‑level expertise published once, credited to each practice's providers.
The same facts everywhereOne phone, address and service list per practice across Google, directories and AI sources.
Back‑end links between sistersResource pages, provider bios and citations that connect nearby practices without rebranding them.
Stays individual: name, logo, website, colors, Google profile, reviews, voice.
Ties together underneath: parent‑company data, AMP's practice pages, shared expertise, consistent facts.

When sisters compete

AI already treats some of your practices as each other's competition.

67 pairs of AMP locations sit within 30 km of each other. Because nothing tells AI they're family, it sometimes answers one practice's question with its sister's name, and the family gets no credit.

Nouveau Day Spa and Synergy MedAesthetics in Kennewick are 5.4 km apart. In Nouveau's searches, AI named its AMP sister instead of Nouveau 7 times.

Ever/Body Hartford and BeautyFix West Hartford are 3.5 km apart. In Ever/Body's searches, AI named BeautyFix instead 6 times. Two AMP brands, splitting one market's trust.

How AI decides

AI trusts what it can confirm. A network confirms itself.

AI doesn't rank a page of links. It reads sources across the web and names the few businesses it can verify from many places at once. We call building that on purpose authority stacking. Wire your 77 practices into one family, and every practice helps vouch for the others.

1. Alone, a practice is a guess

One website, one profile. AI finds a few sources, can't confirm them, and names someone it knows better.

2. Together, they vouch for each other

Behind the scenes: parent-company data in each site's code, AMP's practice pages, shared expert content and matching facts. Each source confirms the others, while every brand stays its own.

3. New practices start ahead

Any practice that joins plugs into the network on day one and gets vouched for by every sister, instead of starting from zero.

This is all we do

We specialize in AI search. Here's what happens under the hood.

Modern AI search doesn't answer from memory alone. It runs retrieval‑augmented generation (RAG): the question is turned into a vector, matched against passages from across the web, and the model writes its answer only from the passages that survive retrieval, reranking and corroboration. A practice that isn't in that retained context can't be named, however good it is.

01

Query decomposition and embedding

The prompt is split into sub‑queries ("botox," "Kennewick," "best," "near me") and each is projected by a transformer encoder into a high‑dimensional space, where meaning is measured as distance.

q → E(q) ∈ ℝd
02

Hybrid dense and sparse retrieval

Nearest‑neighbor search over passage embeddings is fused with keyword (BM25) scoring to pull the top candidate passages from the live web index.

sim(q, c) = E(q)·E(c) / ‖E(q)‖‖E(c)‖
03

Cross‑encoder reranking

Each candidate is re‑scored with the query for relevance, freshness and source authority. Thin, inconsistent or blocked pages fall out here.

r(q, c) = σ(W·[q ⊕ c])
04

Entity resolution and corroboration

Mentions are resolved to real businesses through schema markup, sameAs links and knowledge‑graph IDs. A practice backed by many consistent passages gains confidence; a parent organization that links its practices lends each one its corroboration. Conflicting facts, like two phone numbers, split it into weaker fragments.

conf(e) ∝ Σ agree(ci, cj) + Σsister w·conf(s) − Σ conflict(ci, cj)
05

Grounded generation

The model writes from the retained context and names only businesses above its confidence threshold. Every follow‑up ("which is cheapest," "who's open Saturday") re‑checks the same set.

P(name e | q, C) > θ

Our technique

Semantic Language Alignment

Most agencies optimize pages for keywords. We optimize the whole entity for retrieval. For AMP, that means the network: we lock one true statement of who each practice is and how it belongs to AMP, measure how far every source on the web drifts from it, fix the outliers, then publish new passages shaped like the questions patients actually ask. Everything is bound to AMP in schema, so AI sees one family of 77 practices.

ALGORITHM NetworkAlignment(N, Q, S)
  input   N  the network (AMP + 77 practices)
          Q  patient prompt set per market
          S  every source that mentions N
  output  aligned corpus S*, link graph G

 1  for each p ∈ N:
 2      c_p ← CanonicalStatement(p, parent = AMP)
 3      for each s ∈ S(p):
 4          drift(s) ← 1 − cos(Embed(s), Embed(c_p))
 5          if drift(s) > τ = 0.18 · w(authority(s)):
 6              Rewrite(s, c_p) ∪ Normalize(NAP, schema)
 7  G ← Link(N, sisters within r km, topical hubs)
 8  for each q ∈ Q:
 9      gap_q ← Σ max(0, sim(q,n) − sim(q,S*)) · λ(n)
10      P ← P ∪ Generate(q, c_p, gap_q, Q→A→cite)
11  Bind(S*, parentOrganization(AMP), sameAs(p))
12  repeat monthly until conf(p | q) > θ  ∀ p, q
Proprietary. Parts of this algorithm are redacted.

In plain English: AI only names practices whose facts line up across the web. We make every source say the same true thing about each AMP practice, connect the family behind the scenes without changing any brand, and write it the way patients ask, so your practices land inside the circle.
